slides.headline: THE DOG HARNESS WORKED — PATENT PAPERWORK KILLED IT
slides.body: He sat at a bar 7 years ago and watched a woman's dog wrap itself in its own leash. His fix: a small 3D-printed sliding piece that rides along a cable, so the leash moves with the dog instead of knotting. He tested it on a life-sized stuffed dog — and it worked

slides.headline: EVERY GUIDE HE READ MADE IT SOUND IMPOSSIBLE
slides.body: He needed to search existing patents to check if his idea was new, produce technical drawings a manufacturer would accept, and write a legal specification in the exact format the US Patent Office expects. For 7 years he'd start, get intimidated, and shelve it

slides.headline: AI WROTE THE ENTIRE PATENT FILING IN 2 WEEKS
slides.body: He handed AI his old sketches. It searched existing patents, judged whether the idea was truly new, produced the required technical drawings, and drafted the full legal specification in the exact language the US Patent Office expects. Total filing cost: about $65

slides.headline: HE FILED THIS MONTH WITHOUT EVER CALLING A LAWYER
slides.body: The provisional patent landed at the US Patent Office this month. He does AI engineering for a living but had zero patent experience. He's now building the whole product and company with AI — documenting every step publicly

slides.headline: A TOTAL BEGINNER FILED A REAL PATENT IN 2 WEEKS
slides.body: Every business has work stuck behind an expertise wall — legal filings, technical specs, compliance paperwork. He had zero patent experience and AI carried the whole process to a filed patent in 2 weeks for $65, without a lawyer or a consultant

caption:
He sat on an invention for 7 years — then AI filed the patent in 2 weeks for $65. Swipe for the full story 👆

A man sketched a better dog harness at a bar 7 years ago after watching a dog tangle in its own leash, 3D-printed a sliding piece that lets the leash move with the dog instead of knotting, tested it on a stuffed animal, shelved it because patent paperwork killed his motivation every time he tried, then this month handed his old sketches to AI which searched existing patents, judged novelty, produced technical drawings, and drafted the full legal specification for the US Patent Office — filed for about $65 in 2 weeks with zero patent experience and no lawyer.

Ideas don't die in drawers because nobody wants to build them. They die because the next step needs a specialist. AI just proved it can do that expert work in weeks for pocket change.
